input.reasoning_summary:
The claim states that Apple's total net sales for the quarter ended June 27, 2026 increased by more than 10% year over year. Multiple evidence sources (E2, E4, E11) consistently show total net sales of $109,417 million for Q3 2026 compared to $94,036 million for Q3 2025, representing a 16% increase. This exceeds the 10% threshold stated in the claim.

Challenge H1 (restatements/corrections): No evidence was found of any restatements, corrections, or adjustments to the reported net sales figures that would alter the year-over-year growth calculation.

Challenge H2 (acquisitions/accounting changes): The evidence refutes this challenge. E13 and E14 show that the revenue growth was driven by organic factors - higher sales of existing product lines (iPhone, Services, Mac) and currency effects - not by acquisitions, divestitures, or accounting method changes.

Challenge H3 (one-time events): No evidence was found indicating that the reported net sales growth was driven by one-time events, non-recurring items, or unusual circumstances.

The verdict remains SUPPORTED as the evidence consistently confirms the claim and no contradicting evidence was found.
